130256.problem: A change in the vishvananda/netlink library (v1.2.1) makes interrupted netlink calls return EINTR instead of silently ignoring the flag, causing dropped or incomplete network configuration updates. Under heavy host load this leads to very rare, sporadic network failures on nodes.
130256.affected: Nodes (kubelet) and the pods running on them that rely on netlink‑based network configuration, especially under heavy load conditions.
130256.fix: Wrap netlink calls with a retry mechanism that automatically repeats the operation when it is interrupted (EINTR). This restores the previous tolerant behavior and makes the networking stack resilient to transient interruptions.
130256.impact: Nodes experiencing high CPU or I/O pressure will no longer see intermittent loss of network connectivity for pods or services, improving overall cluster reliability and reducing the need for manual intervention or pod restarts.

130260.problem: NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation (BalancedAllocation) plugin gave a non‑zero score for best‑effort pods that request zero CPU/memory, causing those pods to be treated as if they had resources. This led to many best‑effort pods being scheduled onto the same node, breaking the intended balanced‑allocation behavior.
130260.affected: Clusters using the NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation (BalancedAllocation) scheduler plugin, especially those running best‑effort (zero‑request) pods.
130260.fix: The plugin now detects pods with zero resource requests (best‑effort) and skips them entirely during scoring, so they no longer affect the balanced allocation calculation.
130260.impact: Best‑effort workloads are no longer clustered on a single node, resulting in more even pod distribution and better overall node utilization for clusters that enable the BalancedAllocation plugin.

130328.problem: The /flagz endpoint of kube-apiserver returned flag values in an unparsed format even when the ComponentFlagz feature gate was enabled, making it difficult for clients to interpret the data.
130328.affected: Clients and tools that query the kube-apiserver /flagz endpoint for flag information were receiving unparsed data, potentially leading to misinterpretation.
130328.fix: When the ComponentFlagz feature gate is enabled, /flagz now returns flag values that are correctly parsed, matching the expected format.
130328.impact: Monitoring, debugging, and automation tools that query /flagz can now rely on accurate flag data without additional parsing, improving observability and reducing integration overhead.

130329.affected: Users running Windows workloads and participating in Kubernetes testing activities

130335.problem: When the kubelet was restarted while a user was deleting a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) that was still referenced by a running pod, the kubelet incorrectly unmounted the pod's volumes, causing the pod to lose access to its storage.
130335.affected: Pods with attached PVCs on nodes where the kubelet restarts while the PVC is being deleted.
130335.fix: The kubelet now detects PVCs in the deletion phase that are still in use and skips unmounting their volumes during a kubelet restart, keeping the volumes mounted for running pods.
130335.impact: Running pods that rely on a PVC will no longer experience unexpected volume unmounts and potential data access interruptions when the kubelet restarts, improving workload stability and data availability.

130348.problem: In Kubernetes v1.32 a regression caused nodes to stop reporting their status to the control plane and to fail to renew their serving certificates after the kubelet was restarted.
130348.affected: All cluster nodes running the kubelet that experience a kubelet restart could become unreported and have expired certificates, affecting workloads scheduled on those nodes.
130348.fix: The kubelet logic was corrected so that, after a restart, it reliably sends node status updates and triggers renewal of its serving certificates.
130348.impact: Nodes remain healthy in the API and their serving certificates stay valid, preventing nodes from being marked NotReady and avoiding potential pod eviction or loss of connectivity for components that rely on node certificates.

130394.problem: In the Restricted Pod Security Admission (PSA) profile, the ImageVolume type was not permitted, causing pods that used ImageVolume to be rejected even though they might be safe under the restricted policy.
130394.affected: Users running pods with ImageVolume while using the Restricted PSA profile were unable to create those pods.
130394.fix: The Restricted PSA profile now includes ImageVolume in its allowed volume types, so pods using ImageVolume can be created without violating the profile.
130394.impact: Allows workloads that rely on ImageVolume to run under the most restrictive security posture, reducing the need to relax PSA settings or use work‑arounds.

130398.problem: Recursive fsGroup permission and ownership changes on large volumes can take hours or days, causing workloads to appear stuck. Kubelet only logged that a change was in progress without any progress details, leaving users without actionable information.
130398.affected: Pods that use a volume with an fsGroup setting, especially on large filesystems (e.g., multi‑terabyte NFS or other shared volumes). The kubelet on the node handling the volume is responsible for the change.
130398.fix: Kubelet now tracks and logs progress for volume permission and ownership changes, periodically reporting how much of the file tree has been processed. This gives users visibility into long‑running fsGroup operations.
130398.impact: Operators can now monitor the status of large fsGroup changes, reducing confusion and improving troubleshooting for workloads that use large or NFS volumes. It helps estimate remaining time and confirms that the operation is making progress.

130401.problem: The KUBE_PROXY_NFTABLES_SKIP_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK environment variable was not respected correctly; the nftables proxier would skip the kernel version check even when the variable was unset or empty, leading to unexpected behavior on unsupported kernel versions.
130401.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy with the nftables proxier, especially those relying on the skip‑kernel‑version check environment variable.
130401.fix: The nftables proxier now skips the kernel version check only when the environment variable is explicitly set to a non‑empty value. Users who need to bypass the check must set KUBE_PROXY_NFTABLES_SKIP_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK.
130401.impact: Ensures that kube-proxy’s nftables mode only disables the kernel version safety check when deliberately requested, preventing accidental use on incompatible kernels and restoring expected configuration semantics.

130405.problem: Several built‑in controller roles were missing the `watch` permission, preventing those controllers from watching the resources they manage and causing controller functionality (e.g., CronJob execution, endpoint updates, HPA scaling, node health monitoring, garbage collection, storage version migration) to be broken or degraded.
130405.affected: Clusters where the built‑in controller roles were used without the watch permission; specifically the kube‑controller‑manager controllers listed above.
130405.fix: Added the `watch` verb to the RBAC rules for the listed `system:controller:` roles (cronjob-controller, endpoint-controller, endpointslice-controller, endpointslicemirroring-controller, horizontal-pod-autoscaler, node-controller, pod-garbage-collector, storage-version-migrator-controller).
130405.impact: Controllers can now successfully watch and react to changes in the cluster, restoring expected behavior for cron jobs, service endpoints, autoscaling, node management, garbage collection, and storage version migration.

130450.problem: The CEL CIDR library incorrectly rejected CIDR subnets that are fully contained within another CIDR when using the containsCIDR function, causing validation rules in CRDs to fail for valid nested CIDR ranges.
130450.affected: Anyone defining CRDs with CEL validation rules that compare CIDR ranges (e.g., checking that excludeSubnets are within subnets). The API server validation path is impacted.
130450.fix: The containsCIDR implementation was corrected so that a CIDR that is a subset of another CIDR is correctly recognized as contained.
130450.impact: CRDs that use CEL expressions to validate that one CIDR is within another now work as intended, preventing false validation failures and reducing the need for custom workarounds.

130484.problem: In Kubernetes v1.32, kube-proxy’s cleanup of conntrack entries for Services with ExternalIP or LoadBalancerIP on UDP traffic did not filter by the service destination port. When a Pod with a UDP port changed, kube-proxy attempted to delete *all* UDP conntrack entries for that service, leading to excessive CPU and memory consumption (up to 12 GB RAM and 1.5 CPU cores) and potential OOM crashes.
130484.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes v1.32 with kube-proxy managing Services that have ExternalIP/LoadBalancerIP and expose UDP ports; any Pods that update UDP endpoints trigger the issue.
130484.fix: kube-proxy now correctly filters conntrack cleanup by the Service’s destination port for UDP services, limiting the deletion to only the relevant conntrack entries.
130484.impact: Reduces CPU and memory usage of kube-proxy during UDP service updates, preventing OOM situations and preserving cluster stability for workloads that use UDP (e.g., CoreDNS).

130559.problem: The exclusive assignment availability check for the InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs feature gate was incorrect, causing the feature to be reported as unavailable or to fail when it should have been enabled.
130559.affected: Users who enable the InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs feature gate on nodes—typically workloads that need in‑place vertical pod scaling with exclusive CPU allocation.
130559.fix: Corrected the logic that verifies exclusive CPU assignment availability, ensuring the InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs feature gate correctly detects and uses exclusive CPU resources.
130559.impact: Clusters that enable InPlacePodVerticalScaling with exclusive CPU assignment can now rely on the feature working as documented, allowing safe in‑place vertical scaling of pod CPU resources without fallback or errors.

130574.problem: A race condition could clear the PodResizeStatus 'Proposed' flag. The API server set the status to Proposed when a resize request arrived, but the kubelet later merged its own status and overwrote that flag, causing the resize request to be lost.
130574.affected: Clusters with the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature enabled; pods undergoing in‑place vertical scaling; kubelet and API server interactions.
130574.fix: The API server no longer sets the resize status to Proposed on receipt of a resize request, preventing the kubelet from clobbering the flag and ensuring the status transition is managed correctly.
130574.impact: Pods using the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature will now have reliable resize status updates, eliminating missed or incorrect resize states and improving the stability of in‑place vertical scaling operations.

130616.problem: The tests TestSetVolumeOwnershipOwner for fsGroup=3000 and symlink scenarios were failing because the ownership verification logic reported "invalid owner" when the tests were run as root, due to improper handling of permission changes.
130616.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that run the Kubernetes storage volume unit tests, especially those testing fsGroup and symlink handling on Linux.
130616.fix: Adjusted the file permission change handling in volume_linux_test.go to correctly verify ownership when running as root, fixing the validation logic for both fsGroup and symlink cases.
130616.impact: Ensures the storage volume ownership tests pass in CI and for developers, restoring confidence in the test suite and preventing false negatives that could block releases.

130666.problem: YAML manifests that contain comments (valid YAML but not pure JSON) were sometimes detected as JSON due to a simplistic regex check, causing the decoder to attempt JSON parsing and fail.
130666.affected: Any component that consumes YAML input via the shared yaml decoder – notably kubectl and the kube-apiserver – could reject valid manifests.
130666.fix: The decoder logic now correctly distinguishes YAML from JSON, ensuring that inputs which could be interpreted as JSON are parsed as YAML when appropriate.
130666.impact: Users can reliably apply YAML manifests (including those with comments) via kubectl or the API server without encountering spurious parse errors, improving stability of configuration workflows.

130831.problem: In-place pod vertical scaling could modify a container's swap limit. Swap handling in the kubelet is not fully supported, and resizing swap can lead to undefined behavior or node instability, especially for containers that do not use the RestartContainer memory ResizePolicy.
130831.affected: Pods using InPlacePodVerticalScaling (beta) where containers have swap enabled and a memory ResizePolicy other than RestartContainer.
130831.fix: The kubelet now disables in-place pod resize for any container that has swap enabled and does not specify a memory ResizePolicy of RestartContainer. The check is added to IsInPlacePodVerticalScalingAllowed, preventing such resizes from being attempted.
130831.impact: Users attempting in‑place vertical scaling on pods with swap‑enabled containers will no longer succeed; the operation will be blocked or fall back to a restart. This avoids potential node issues and makes the behavior predictable, improving cluster stability.

130875.problem: The godoc example for JWT authenticator validation omitted an explicit boolean comparison for the `email_verified` claim, causing type‑checking to miss non‑boolean values and potentially allowing misconfiguration.
130875.affected: Users configuring JWT authentication (e.g., setting `username.expression` to `claims.email`) who rely on the documentation for correct claim validation rules.
130875.fix: Updated the documentation example to use `claims.?email_verified.orValue(true) == true`, ensuring the expression is type‑checked as a boolean and that non‑boolean `email_verified` claims are caught at runtime.
130875.impact: Provides correct guidance for configuring JWT authenticators, helping users set up proper claim validation and avoiding subtle authentication bugs caused by improper claim types.

131020.problem: When a watch event could not be decrypted, kube-apiserver still emitted subsequent watch events, breaking the guarantee that a watch stream stops on decryption errors and potentially delivering out‑of‑order or inconsistent data.
131020.affected: Clients consuming watch streams (controllers, kubelet, custom operators) that rely on correct decryption of encrypted resources.
131020.fix: The apiserver now halts emission of further watch events after a decryption failure, ensuring the watch stream is terminated or handled correctly instead of continuing with possibly malformed data.
131020.impact: Clients that watch resources (e.g., controllers, operators, kubectl) receive a correct and consistent event stream, preventing hidden errors and maintaining security/consistency guarantees for encrypted objects such as Secrets.

131036.problem: When kube-apiserver is started with --anonymous-auth=false and the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate is enabled, kubeadm's health check could not authenticate to the apiserver, causing the health check to fail and control‑plane initialization to stall.
131036.affected: Kubernetes clusters initialized with kubeadm where the apiserver has --anonymous-auth=false and the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate is enabled.
131036.fix: kubeadm now performs the kube‑apiserver health check using an authenticated request (or bypasses the anonymous check) when anonymous authentication is disabled and the feature gate is on, ensuring the health endpoint can be reached.
131036.impact: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm that disable anonymous authentication will no longer get stuck waiting for the apiserver to become healthy, improving reliability of init/join operations and control‑plane readiness detection.

131263.problem: When the kube-apiserver flag --service-cluster-ip-range was changed from a single‑stack range to a dual‑stack range, the default ServiceCIDR API object could not be updated and dual‑stack Service objects could not be created.
131263.affected: Clusters that were originally configured with a single‑stack service CIDR and later switched the --service-cluster-ip-range flag to dual‑stack; any workloads trying to create dual‑stack Services.
131263.fix: kube-apiserver now correctly updates the default ServiceCIDR object and allows creation of dual‑stack Service resources after the flag is changed to include both IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs.
131263.impact: Enables clusters to transition to dual‑stack networking without having to reinstall or recreate the cluster, allowing IPv4/IPv6 services to be created and used.

124360.problem: Cluster administrators could not limit the number of PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) that use a specific VolumeAttributesClass, making it impossible to enforce quota policies based on storage attribute classes.
124360.affected: Cluster admins who need to enforce storage quotas and workloads that create PVCs with a VolumeAttributesClass.
124360.fix: Introduces a new ResourceQuota scope name `VolumeAttributesClass`. PVC objects that specify a VolumeAttributesClass are matched by this scope, and admins can create a ResourceQuota with `scopeName: VolumeAttributesClass` and appropriate `matchExpressions` to count and limit PVCs per class.
124360.impact: Enables fine‑grained quota enforcement for storage resources, preventing over‑provisioning of PVCs with particular attribute classes and helping clusters stay within intended storage limits.

125230.problem: kubectl had no mechanism to specify user preferences (e.g., output format, pagination) separate from the cluster authentication data in kubeconfig, forcing users to repeat flags or use work‑arounds.
125230.affected: All users of the kubectl command who want to set persistent client‑side preferences; especially those who currently rely on scripts or repeated flag usage.
125230.fix: Introduces an alpha‑stage `kuberc` file that lives alongside kubeconfig. kubectl reads preferences from this file to customize its default behavior (output, column widths, paging, etc.) without affecting cluster credentials.
125230.impact: Makes kubectl more ergonomic for developers and operators by allowing persistent, per‑user defaults, reducing the need for repetitive flag usage and scripts. Improves day‑to‑day productivity when interacting with clusters.

127577.problem: When users specified custom values for some eviction thresholds (evictionHard, evictionSoft, evictionSoftGracePeriod, evictionMinimumReclaim) in the kubelet configuration, the unspecified thresholds were reset to zero instead of keeping their built‑in defaults, leading to unexpected eviction behavior.
127577.affected: Clusters that customize kubelet eviction settings; any workloads relying on proper eviction thresholds for memory, node filesystem, and image filesystem pressure.
127577.fix: Introduce mergeDefaultEvictionSettings which merges the built‑in default eviction settings with the user‑provided configuration. User‑specified signals overwrite defaults, while any signal not set by the user inherits the default value.
127577.impact: Ensures that customizing only a subset of eviction parameters does not unintentionally disable other eviction checks. This prevents premature pod evictions or lack of eviction protection, making kubelet resource‑pressure handling reliable for all clusters.

127897.problem: X.509 client certificate authentication did not populate the user UID field, leaving it empty for authorizers and admission plugins that rely on UID for policy decisions.
127897.affected: Clusters using X.509 client certificates for authentication (e.g., kubectl, kubelet, or any component that talks to the API server with client certs) where UID‑based authorization or admission logic is needed.
127897.fix: Kubernetes components that accept X.509 client certificates now extract a UID from a subject name RDN with OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.57683.2 (a single string value). This behavior can be disabled via the beta feature gate `AllowParsingUserUIDFromCertAuth` until it graduates to GA.
127897.impact: Authorizers and admission controllers receive the correct UID for X.509‑authenticated users, enabling UID‑based RBAC and admission policies to work as intended.

128152.problem: After the kubelet upgrade, it now tracks images and the authentication data that allowed those images to be pulled and persists this information. When an image requires credentials, the kubelet forces a pull if it does not have the stored auth data, even if the pod’s imagePullPolicy is IfNotPresent or Never. This can cause pods that rely on a locally cached image (Never) to fail to start after a node reboot or kubelet restart because the required auth data is missing.
128152.affected: Pods that use imagePullPolicy=Never or IfNotPresent for images that require authentication, especially after a node reboot or kubelet restart, may fail to start because the kubelet attempts a new pull when auth data is not present.
128152.fix: Introduces a new kubelet configuration option that enables tracking of image‑pull authentication data and persists it across reboots. The kubelet now enforces re‑authentication for images that need credentials, ensuring that any missing auth information triggers a pull attempt, aligning image pulls with current credentials.
128152.impact: Improves security by guaranteeing that images requiring credentials are always pulled with up‑to‑date authentication, preventing stale or unauthorized images from being used. However, workloads that depend on Never pull policy or rely on cached images without storing auth info may experience startup failures after node restarts, so operators may need to adjust imagePullPolicy or provide persistent auth data.

128184.problem: The existing VolumeCapacityPriority feature preferred nodes with the least allocatable storage, leading to suboptimal pod placement for dynamically provisioned volumes.
128184.affected: Pods that request PersistentVolumeClaims with dynamic provisioning and the scheduler's node‑selection logic.
128184.fix: Introduces the StorageCapacityScoring feature gate (alpha, disabled by default) that replaces VolumeCapacityPriority and scores nodes by their available storage capacity, preferring nodes with the maximum allocatable storage for dynamic provisioning.
128184.impact: Improves scheduler decision‑making for pods that request storage, resulting in better storage utilization and reduced risk of filling up nodes. Clusters using dynamic provisioning will see more efficient pod placement once the feature is enabled.

128367.problem: Pod sidecar containers could not be resized in-place, requiring a pod restart to change CPU/memory resources, which caused downtime and limited dynamic scaling for workloads that use sidecars.
128367.affected: Workloads that include sidecar containers and need to change CPU/memory resources at runtime, e.g., pods using service‑mesh proxies, log/metric sidecars, or any sidecar‑based architecture.
128367.fix: Implemented in-place vertical scaling support for sidecar containers (containers defined in initContainers with restartPolicy Always). The kubelet now applies resource updates to these sidecars without restarting the pod.
128367.impact: Allows users to adjust resources of sidecar containers on the fly, reducing disruption and improving the effectiveness of autoscaling and performance tuning for workloads that rely on sidecars such as service meshes, logging agents, and monitoring agents.

128372.problem: The kubelet credential provider could not supply a service account token (with a specific audience) and related KSA annotations to image credential provider plugins, limiting authentication options for pulling images that require such tokens.
128372.affected: Clusters that use kubelet image credential provider plugins and need to authenticate image pulls with service account tokens; pods pulling images from registries that require such tokens; administrators configuring these plugins.
128372.fix: Added an optional `tokenAttribute` field to the on‑disk kubelet credential provider configuration. When set, the kubelet generates a KSA token bound to the specified audience and includes configurable KSA annotations, sending both to the credential provider plugin via stdin alongside existing image information.
128372.impact: Enables image credential provider plugins to authenticate using pod‑bound service account tokens, supporting registries that require audience‑scoped tokens and improving security and flexibility of image pulls.

128499.problem: The ClusterTrustBundle API was not available at the v1beta1 version, preventing the ClusterTrustBundleProjection feature from functioning on the kubelet side unless the kubelet was restarted after the API became available.
128499.affected: Kubelet processes on nodes that use the ClusterTrustBundleProjection feature and clusters where the ClusterTrustBundle API version changes.
128499.fix: The ClusterTrustBundle API is promoted to v1beta1 and the ClusterTrustBundleProjection feature gate is required to be enabled. If the API appears after the kubelet has started, a kubelet restart is needed to activate the feature.
128499.impact: Enables pods to use projected volumes that reference cluster-wide trust bundles, improving secure certificate distribution and simplifying workload authentication.

128546.problem: Deployments and ReplicaSets did not expose the number of pods that were in the terminating phase, making it difficult to monitor rollouts and understand pod termination progress.
128546.affected: Users and tooling that rely on Deployment or ReplicaSet status for monitoring or automation, especially during rolling updates, are now able to see terminating replica counts.
128546.fix: Added a new status field `.status.terminatingReplicas` to the Deployment and ReplicaSet APIs. The field is populated when the `DeploymentPodReplacementPolicy` (aka DeploymentReplicaSetTerminatingReplicas) feature gate is enabled, allowing the API to report how many replicas are currently terminating.
128546.impact: Provides better observability of rollout progress and termination behavior, enabling controllers, dashboards, and scripts to accurately track terminating pods and make more informed decisions during updates.

128586.problem: Device resource claims could only specify a single selection criterion, preventing users from expressing alternative devices or prioritizing multiple criteria for satisfying a device request.
128586.affected: Pods and workloads that use DRA via ResourceClaims (e.g., GPU‑enabled applications) and cluster administrators defining device selection policies.
128586.fix: Adds support for a "one-of" prioritized list of selection criteria in a Device Resource Allocation (DRA) claim. The claim can now include multiple selectors ordered by preference, and the scheduler (and related DRA components) will evaluate them sequentially until a matching device is found.
128586.impact: Provides flexible device allocation for workloads that can run on any device from a set, reducing the need for multiple claims or manual selection, and improves scheduling success rates for GPU, NIC, and other device‑backed pods.

128786.problem: The API server accepted IP and CIDR values with non‑standard formatting (e.g., extra leading zeros like "192.168.000.005"), which could lead to security problems and will be rejected in a future release.
128786.affected: Any workload or resource that includes IP address or CIDR fields (e.g., Services, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, Pod spec) created with non‑standard formatting.
128786.fix: The apiserver now validates IP/CIDR fields and returns a warning when an object is created with an invalid format, alerting users before the value is forbidden.
128786.impact: Users creating Pods, Services, NetworkPolicies, etc., with malformed IP/CIDR strings will see warnings, allowing them to correct the values now and avoid future failures, improving security and consistency of network configurations.

128857.problem: Kubelet did not expose its command-line flags through an HTTP endpoint, making it hard for operators and monitoring tools to view current flag settings without accessing the node directly.
128857.affected: Cluster administrators, monitoring systems, and any tooling that needs to inspect kubelet flags remotely.
128857.fix: Introduces a new `/flagz` HTTP endpoint on the kubelet server that returns the current flag values in a human‑readable form.
128857.impact: Simplifies debugging and observability of kubelet configuration, allowing automated tools and operators to retrieve flag settings remotely without SSH or node‑level commands.

128971.problem: Clusters that manage Service CIDR need a way to define multiple Service CIDRs via an API object and enforce constraints (e.g., no overlap, specific IP ranges) while retaining the option to keep a single ServiceCIDR per cluster.
128971.affected: Cluster administrators and Kubernetes distributions that manage the cluster Service CIDR; workloads that rely on service IP allocation.
128971.fix: Graduated the MultiCIDRServiceAllocator feature gate to stable and added the DisableAllocatorDualWrite gate to beta (off by default). This introduces the ServiceCIDR API object for defining cluster Service CIDRs and allows administrators to use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy to enforce CIDR constraints or preserve single‑CIDR behavior.
128971.impact: Enables flexible, multi‑CIDR service IP allocation and policy‑driven validation, improving network planning and security. Distributions and administrators must review and possibly adjust their configurations because the feature gates have changed.

129407.problem: When a client requests a list of resources with the response format set to Protobuf, the API server marshalled the entire list in memory before sending it. This caused high memory consumption and could lead to OOM for large collections.
129407.affected: Clients that request list operations in Protobuf format, especially when the list size is large. This includes any workloads or tools that perform bulk reads via the API server.
129407.fix: The API server now streams Protobuf list responses, marshaling each element individually. This reduces peak memory usage for large list calls. The behavior can be turned off with the `StreamingCollectionEncodingToProtobuf` feature gate.
129407.impact: Clusters that serve large list responses (e.g., many pods, nodes, or custom resources) use less memory, improving stability and allowing higher scale without risking out‑of‑memory errors.

129543.problem: The DRA API limited the number of pods that could share a single ResourceClaim to 32, preventing larger workloads from using the same claim. Additionally, downgrading a cluster that has used the new higher limit would fail because older versions reject ResourceClaims with more than 32 entries in status.reservedFor.
129543.affected: Workloads that use the Device Resource Allocation (DRA) API and share a ResourceClaim across many pods, as well as cluster operators planning version downgrades.
129543.fix: The maximum number of pods that can reference the same ResourceClaim has been raised to 256. Clusters can now safely schedule up to 256 pods per claim, but downgrades to Kubernetes 1.32.0 are not supported when the limit is exceeded.
129543.impact: Enables high‑density workloads and advanced use‑cases (e.g., large stateful sets or batch jobs) to share a ResourceClaim, improving resource utilization. Administrators must avoid downgrading clusters that exceed the old limit, otherwise the apiserver will reject updates to ResourceClaims.

129770.problem: The AnyVolumeDataSource feature was in beta and required a feature gate to be enabled, preventing users from reliably using arbitrary volume data sources such as CSI populator or snapshots.
129770.affected: Workloads that use PersistentVolumeClaims with a dataSource (e.g., CSI drivers, snapshot restore, PVC-to-PVC copy) and developers of storage solutions.
129770.fix: Promoted the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate to GA, making it enabled by default and stabilizing the API for specifying any VolumeDataSource in PersistentVolumeClaims.
129770.impact: Enables production workloads to use volume data sources without extra configuration, simplifying CSI volume population and snapshot use, and reducing operational overhead.

129954.problem: Kubernetes did not include a node's swap capacity in the node.status.nodeSystemInfo field, so users and tools could not retrieve swap information via the API.
129954.affected: All clusters where swap is enabled on nodes; operators, monitoring systems, and any automation that queries node status for resource information.
129954.fix: The node status now includes the swap capacity (total swap bytes) in node.status.nodeSystemInfo, populated by the kubelet and exposed through the API server.
129954.impact: Cluster operators and monitoring tools can now see swap capacity for each node via kubectl or the API, enabling better resource visibility and decision‑making around workloads that consider swap usage.

129970.problem: The resource.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version is deprecated and will be removed in Kubernetes 1.36, causing any workloads or controllers that still use this version to fail once the removal occurs.
129970.affected: Clusters that have custom resources, controllers, or workloads using the DRA v1beta1 API (e.g., Device, CapacityPool, CounterSet) will encounter errors after 1.36.
129970.fix: Migrate all usages of the DRA (Device Resource Allocation) API to the newer resource.k8s.io/v1beta2 version, which includes flattened Device fields, renamed CapacityPool/CounterSet fields, and updated plural naming conventions.
129970.impact: Pre‑emptive migration avoids breaking changes after the 1.36 release, ensures compatibility with the improved v1beta2 schema, and keeps clusters stable when the old API is finally removed.

130007.problem: The CSINode.Spec.Drivers[*].Allocatable.Count field was immutable, so when a CSI driver’s volume capacity changed the node’s reported allocatable volume count could become stale. The kube-scheduler continued to use the outdated value, causing stateful pods that need volumes to remain unschedulable.
130007.affected: Clusters using CSI drivers that report changing volume capacity, especially workloads with stateful pods that depend on accurate allocatable volume counts.
130007.fix: Introduced an alpha feature gate `MutableCSINodeAllocatableCount` that makes the Allocatable.Count field mutable and adds the `NodeAllocatableUpdatePeriodSeconds` field to the CSIDriver object. When enabled, the kubelet can periodically update the node’s allocatable volume capacity, keeping scheduler information current.
130007.impact: Prevents stateful workloads (e.g., StatefulSets, pods with PVCs) from getting stuck due to stale volume capacity data, improving scheduling correctness and cluster reliability for clusters that use CSI drivers with dynamic capacity.

130028.problem: Kubelet lacked a configurable option to limit the number of subordinate UID/GID IDs (subids) allocated to each pod, making it difficult to control user namespace resource usage and potentially causing conflicts or security concerns.
130028.affected: Kubernetes administrators and workloads that rely on user namespaces for UID/GID isolation; pods that request user namespace mappings.
130028.fix: Introduced a new KubeletConfiguration field `subidsPerPod` that lets administrators specify the number of subuid/subgid IDs to assign to each pod when using user namespaces.
130028.impact: Clusters can now fine‑tune subuid/subgid allocation per pod, preventing exhaustion of subid pools, improving security isolation, and simplifying compliance with environments that require strict user namespace limits.

130116.problem: Recursive Read‑only (RRO) mount support was only available as an alpha/beta feature, so production workloads could not rely on it for enforcing read‑only access to volume subpaths.
130116.affected: Any pod that uses volumes and wants to enforce read‑only access for the entire directory tree, especially security‑focused or compliance‑oriented workloads.
130116.fix: The RRO mount feature has been promoted to GA. Kubelet now treats recursive read‑only mounts as stable, enabling pods to request read‑only access that propagates to all nested directories without additional workarounds.
130116.impact: Clusters can now enforce stricter filesystem security for pods in production, reducing the need for init containers or custom scripts, and improving compliance and reliability of workloads that require immutable filesystems.

130135.problem: Image volume sources were only alpha and did not support subPath/subPathExpr, limiting users from mounting specific directories within an image volume. Additionally, there were no kubelet metrics to observe how often image volumes were requested or successfully mounted, hindering observability.
130135.affected: Workloads that use image volume sources (e.g., Pods) and operators monitoring kubelet metrics.
130135.fix: The image volume source graduated to beta and now permits the use of `subPath` and `subPathExpr`. Three new kubelet metrics (`kubelet_image_volume_requested_total`, `kubelet_image_volume_mounted_succeed_total`, `kubelet_image_volume_mounted_errors_total`) were added to track image volume usage and mounting outcomes.
130135.impact: Users can now mount only the needed subdirectory of an image volume, simplifying pod configurations and reducing unnecessary data exposure. Cluster operators gain visibility into image volume lifecycle through new metrics, aiding troubleshooting and capacity planning.

130183.problem: When using InPlacePodVerticalScaling, decreasing a container's memory limit fails unless the pod's memory resize restartPolicy is set to `RestartContainer`. Additionally, the container's `resources.resizePolicy` field became immutable, preventing users from changing the policy after pod creation.
130183.affected: Workloads that use InPlacePodVerticalScaling to adjust memory limits, especially those that attempted to lower memory without a restart policy, and any pod spec that tried to modify `resources.resizePolicy` after creation.
130183.fix: The control plane now enforces that memory limit reductions are only allowed with `RestartContainer` as the restartPolicy, and the `resizePolicy` field is marked immutable to prevent further modifications. Users must set the desired restartPolicy at pod creation time.
130183.impact: Users who rely on in‑place vertical scaling to downscale memory without restarting containers can no longer do so; they must configure `RestartContainer` up front. The change prevents silent misconfiguration of resize policies and makes the behavior explicit.

130225.problem: Any user could create ResourceClaim or ResourceClaimTemplate objects with the adminAccess field and reference them in pods or deployments, potentially granting privileged resource access without proper authorization.
130225.affected: Users and workloads that create or reference ResourceClaim/ResourceClaimTemplate objects with the adminAccess field without proper admin‑namespace permissions. Administrators must label an admin namespace and adjust RBAC accordingly.
130225.fix: Kubernetes 1.33 enforces that only users who have access to a namespace labeled with `resource.k8s.io/admin-access` can create ResourceClaim or ResourceClaimTemplate objects containing the adminAccess field in that namespace, and only those users may reference these objects in pod or deployment specs.
130225.impact: Adds a security boundary for Dynamic Resource Allocation admin‑access claims, preventing unauthorized privilege escalation. Clusters must label an admin namespace and grant users access before they can use adminAccess, so existing workloads that relied on unrestricted adminAccess may need to be updated.

130291.problem: Kubernetes lacked an API object to represent a LeaseCandidate, which is needed for advanced lease/leader election mechanisms.
130291.affected: Components that perform leader election or work with Lease objects (e.g., controller-manager, scheduler extensions) can now use a dedicated LeaseCandidate resource.
130291.fix: Introduced a new API type `coordination.k8s.io/v1beta1/LeaseCandidate` that can be created, read, updated, and deleted via the API server, allowing components to manage lease candidates via a structured object.
130291.impact: Provides a formal API for lease candidate management, enabling new controller implementations and improving interoperability for leader election scenarios.

130352.problem: When the PodObservedGenerationTracking feature gate was enabled, kubelet did not set the pod's status.observedGeneration, leaving it empty or outdated and preventing users and controllers from seeing which pod spec generation had been observed.
130352.affected: All Pods scheduled on nodes where the kubelet runs with the PodObservedGenerationTracking feature gate enabled; any controller logic that checks status.observedGeneration.
130352.fix: The kubelet now populates status.observedGeneration with the latest metadata.generation it has observed for each pod when the feature gate is turned on.
130352.impact: Controllers and users can reliably compare status.observedGeneration to spec.generation, enabling correct detection of pod updates, improving rollout logic and debugging of pod state mismatches.

130447.problem: There was no way for DRA drivers or administrators to mark a device as unusable, so unhealthy or decommissioned devices could still be allocated to pods, leading to failures or sub‑optimal usage.
130447.affected: Clusters using DRA drivers or administrators managing device resources; workloads that request devices via DRA device claims.
130447.fix: Introduced device taints in DRA. Drivers or admins can now apply a taint to a device to mark it unusable, which prevents the scheduler from allocating new pods to that device. At runtime, pods with claims that do not tolerate the taint can be evicted, with behavior governed by the taint severity.
130447.impact: Improves reliability and operational control of device resources. Unhealthy or retired devices are automatically excluded from scheduling, and workloads can be safely evicted when a device becomes unusable, reducing failure rates and simplifying device lifecycle management.

130463.problem: The MatchLabelKeys and MismatchLabelKeys options for PodAffinity and PodAntiAffinity were only available as an alpha/beta feature behind a feature gate, limiting their use in production workloads.
130463.affected: Users and operators that define PodAffinity/PodAntiAffinity rules with MatchLabelKeys or MismatchLabelKeys, as well as workloads that depend on these rules for pod placement.
130463.fix: The feature is graduated to GA, removing the feature gate and making the label-key matching behavior part of the stable API for pod affinity/anti-affinity.
130463.impact: Clusters can now rely on stable, fully‑supported label‑key matching for pod placement without extra configuration, enabling broader production use of advanced affinity rules.

130536.problem: JobSuccessPolicy was only available as an alpha/beta feature, requiring a feature gate and lacking guaranteed API stability, which limited its adoption for users needing reliable job completion behavior.
130536.affected: Clusters using Job objects that want to control success criteria for job completion. Previously required enabling the JobSuccessPolicy feature gate; now works out‑of‑the‑box.
130536.fix: Promoted JobSuccessPolicy to Stable, removing the feature gate requirement and guaranteeing API stability for the field that controls job success completion semantics.
130536.impact: Users can now rely on the JobSuccessPolicy field in Job specifications without enabling experimental features, simplifying job definitions and improving confidence in job success handling across clusters.

130556.problem: Containers could only be stopped with the default SIGTERM signal, making it impossible for applications that require a different termination signal to shut down gracefully.
130556.affected: Any pod that needs a custom termination signal (e.g., legacy applications, language runtimes with special shutdown handling) and cluster administrators who want finer‑grained control over container termination.
130556.fix: Introduces a new `StopSignal` field in the container lifecycle API, allowing users to specify a custom POSIX signal that kubelet will send when terminating a container.
130556.impact: Improves shutdown semantics for workloads that depend on non‑SIGTERM signals, reducing unwanted restarts or data loss during pod termination and simplifying migration of existing applications to Kubernetes.

130573.problem: Pod condition objects did not include the observedGeneration field, making it impossible for controllers and users to know whether a condition reflects the current pod spec generation.
130573.affected: All workloads that rely on pod conditions for status decisions (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets, custom controllers) and any node running the kubelet with the feature gate enabled, including Windows nodes.
130573.fix: When the PodObservedGenerationTracking feature gate is enabled, the kubelet now populates the observedGeneration field on pod conditions, aligning them with the pod's generation.
130573.impact: Controllers and users can reliably correlate pod conditions with the specific pod generation they pertain to, improving correctness of status handling, rollouts, and debugging.

130577.problem: Hugepage resources could only be requested at the container level, preventing users from declaring pod‑level hugepage allocations and making it harder to schedule and manage workloads that need hugepages across multiple containers.
130577.affected: Workloads that need hugepage memory across containers, such as high‑performance or database workloads, and any cluster operators configuring hugepages.
130577.fix: The Pod API was updated to allow hugepage resources to be specified in the pod spec (spec.resources), enabling pod‑level hugepage requests and limits.
130577.impact: Users can now request hugepages for an entire pod, simplifying configuration and improving scheduler visibility for hugepage requirements, which leads to more reliable placement of workloads that rely on hugepages.

130649.problem: When the PodObservedGenerationTracking feature gate was disabled, kube-scheduler did not populate the `observedGeneration` field on pod conditions. This made it impossible for controllers and users to know which generation of the pod spec a condition referred to, leading to potential mis‑interpretation of pod status.
130649.affected: All workloads that rely on pod condition status, such as controllers, operators, and users monitoring pod health, especially when the feature gate is enabled.
130649.fix: The scheduler now sets the `observedGeneration` field on pod conditions whenever the `PodObservedGenerationTracking` feature gate is enabled, ensuring the condition reflects the generation that triggered it.
130649.impact: Provides accurate tracking of pod condition generations, enabling controllers and operators to make correct decisions based on pod status and paving the way for future features that rely on generation awareness.

130650.problem: Pod conditions did not include the `observedGeneration` field, making it impossible for controllers and users to know which pod spec generation a condition reflects.
130650.affected: Controllers and workloads that read pod conditions (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets, custom controllers) gain accurate generation tracking.
130650.fix: When the `PodObservedGenerationTracking` feature gate is enabled, the kube‑controller‑manager now populates `observedGeneration` on pod conditions.
130650.impact: Enables reliable tracking of condition updates against pod spec generations, improving controller logic, debugging, and observability for workloads that rely on pod conditions.

130658.problem: Job resources lacked a conformance test for the new JobSuccessPolicy, making it hard to verify that clusters correctly implement the success-completion semantics.
130658.affected: Users creating or managing Job objects that rely on the success‑completion policy, as well as cluster vendors who need to pass conformance testing.
130658.fix: Added an end‑to‑end (E2E) test for JobSuccessPolicy to the Kubernetes conformance suite, promoting the feature to required conformance validation.
130658.impact: Clusters must now support and correctly enforce the JobSuccessPolicy, giving users confidence that jobs will behave as documented across all compliant Kubernetes implementations.

130725.problem: ReplicationController objects did not have declarative validation for the `replicas` and `minReadySeconds` fields, causing potential mismatches with existing validation logic and missing required‑field checks.
130725.affected: Users creating or updating ReplicationController objects; the change affects validation performed by the kube-apiserver.
130725.fix: Moved minimum‑value and required‑field validation for `replicas` and `minReadySeconds` to the declarative validation framework. When the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is enabled, any divergence from the old validation is reported via metrics. When `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` is enabled, declarative validation becomes the primary source of errors for these fields.
130725.impact: Provides consistent, observable validation for ReplicationController specs. Users with the feature gates turned on receive accurate error messages and metric visibility, reducing the chance of creating invalid ReplicationController configurations.

130733.problem: The pod .status.resize field was prone to race conditions and ambiguous state representation, allowing conflicting resize statuses and making it difficult for users and controllers to reliably determine the progress of in‑place vertical scaling.
130733.affected: Any workload or automation that inspected pod.status.resize to determine resize state (e.g., custom controllers, monitoring dashboards, scripts) will need to switch to checking the new PodResizeInProgress and PodResizePending conditions.
130733.fix: The .status.resize field is deprecated and will no longer be set. Two new pod conditions, PodResizeInProgress and PodResizePending, are introduced to explicitly convey resize progress, eliminating the race‑prone field and providing a clear, singular source of truth for resize state.
130733.impact: Controllers, monitoring tools, and users can now reliably track pod vertical scaling without encountering overwritten or contradictory status values, improving reliability of in‑place scaling workflows and reducing debugging effort.

130751.problem: Prior to this release, coordinated leader election was only available as an alpha feature without a stable API, limiting its use in production and making leader election less reliable for control-plane components.
130751.affected: Control‑plane components that rely on leader election, such as kube‑controller‑manager and kube‑scheduler, and any custom controllers using the leader election library.
130751.fix: Introduces the new API type `coordination.k8s.io/v1beta1/LeaseCandidate` and promotes the CoordinatedLeaderElection feature to beta, providing a stable API for coordinated leader election.
130751.impact: Control‑plane components (e.g., kube‑controller‑manager, kube‑scheduler) can now use a more robust, production‑ready leader election mechanism, reducing split‑brain scenarios and improving availability during component restarts or upgrades.

130764.problem: Kubernetes did not support allocating partitionable devices (e.g., GPU slices) through the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) framework, preventing workloads from requesting sub‑device resources.
130764.affected: Clusters that use the DRA framework and have partitionable devices; workloads that require sub‑device allocation will benefit once the feature gate is enabled.
130764.fix: Introduced the feature gate `DRAPartitionableDevices`. When enabled, DRA can allocate partitionable devices, exposing the capability to the scheduler and kubelet.
130764.impact: Clusters can now schedule workloads that need only a portion of a device, improving device utilization and enabling new use‑cases such as GPU sharing or FPGA slicing.

130797.problem: HorizontalPodAutoscalers could only use a single cluster-wide tolerance setting, preventing workloads with different scaling sensitivity from configuring their own tolerance thresholds.
130797.affected: Any workload using a HorizontalPodAutoscaler that needs custom tolerance values; all clusters where the alpha gate is enabled.
130797.fix: Introduces an optional `tolerance` field in the HPA spec (under `behavior.scaleUp` and `behavior.scaleDown`) that overrides the controller-manager's default tolerance. The feature is gated behind the `HPAConfigurableTolerance` alpha gate.
130797.impact: Enables per‑HPA tuning of scale‑up and scale‑down tolerance, giving operators finer control over scaling aggressiveness for different applications and reducing unwanted scaling churn.

130844.problem: Clusters could not express a preference to route Service traffic to an endpoint on the same node as the client, limiting locality optimization and increasing cross‑node network traffic.
130844.affected: Any cluster that enables the PreferSameTrafficDistribution feature gate and uses Services with the new trafficDistribution values. Particularly useful for workloads that benefit from node‑local traffic (e.g., sidecar proxies, local caches).
130844.fix: Introduces a new trafficDistribution option `PreferSameNode` (available when the PreferSameTrafficDistribution feature gate is enabled) that tries to always select an endpoint on the same node as the client. Also adds `PreferSameZone` as an alias for the existing `PreferClose` mode.
130844.impact: Enables node‑local service routing, reducing latency and network hop count for workloads that benefit from same‑node communication, and can lower bandwidth usage in multi‑zone clusters. Users can now opt‑in to this behavior via the feature gate.

130880.problem: When the InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus feature gate was disabled, the AllocatedResources field in ContainerStatus could still be read, causing the scheduler to calculate pod resource requests using max(spec, status) while the kubelet used only allocated resources. This mismatch could lead to the scheduler thinking resources were available while the kubelet rejected the pod with OutOfCPU/Memory errors during in‑place vertical scaling operations.
130880.affected: Pods performing in‑place vertical scaling (upsize or downsize) when the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate is disabled; the scheduler and kubelet resource calculations were inconsistent.
130880.fix: The deprecated InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus gate is removed and the AllocatedResources field is now guarded by the primary InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate. When that gate is off, the field is hidden, ensuring both scheduler and kubelet use the same resource view.
130880.impact: Prevents scheduling and admission mismatches for pods that use in‑place vertical scaling, eliminating unexpected pod rejections and improving reliability of resource resizing operations.

130920.problem: The NodeInclusionPolicy field for PodTopologySpread constraints was only available in alpha/beta, so users could not rely on it for production workloads.
130920.affected: Any workloads that use pod topology spread constraints with the NodeInclusionPolicy field, as well as developers relying on a stable API for pod placement logic.
130920.fix: Promoted NodeInclusionPolicyInPodTopologySpread to GA (Stable) in v1.33, making the field stable, updating documentation, and ensuring its behavior is fully supported by the scheduler.
130920.impact: Clusters can now use the NodeInclusionPolicy in pod topology spread constraints in production with confidence, improving pod placement control and reducing the need for work‑arounds.

127053.problem: The kube-apiserver ignored the incoming trace context on authenticated API requests, causing each re‑entrant call to start a new trace instead of being linked as child spans. This broke end‑to‑end distributed tracing for internal components.
127053.affected: Any workload that makes authenticated, re‑entrant calls to the API server (e.g., controllers, admission webhooks, internal components) saw broken trace graphs.
127053.fix: The apiserver now respects and propagates the incoming OpenTelemetry trace context for authenticated requests, linking internal/re‑entrant calls to the original trace instead of creating separate traces.
127053.impact: Provides accurate, contiguous traces across nested API calls, improving observability and debugging of performance or reliability issues in clusters that use distributed tracing.

127092.problem: Pods that need to know the node's topology (zone, region, hostname) had to request permission to get full Node objects, exposing more data than necessary and complicating RBAC.
127092.affected: Pods that require node topology information (e.g., zone, region, hostname) and the users/operators configuring them, especially those running with limited permissions.
127092.fix: The API server now automatically copies the `topology.k8s.io/zone`, `topology.k8s.io/region` and `kubernetes.io/hostname` labels from a Node onto the Pod during the `pods/binding` call, making them available via the downward API.
127092.impact: Applications can retrieve essential node topology information through the downward API without extra RBAC permissions, improving security (least‑privilege) and simplifying topology‑aware workloads.

127709.problem: The previous BackoffManager in client-go/rest did not accept a context, preventing callers from interrupting sleep during backoff and limiting contextual logging support.
127709.affected: Any component or controller that uses client-go REST calls and the BackoffManager, including custom controllers, kubectl, and other Kubernetes clients.
127709.fix: Implemented full contextual logging support in client-go/rest and introduced BackoffManagerWithContext, which respects the caller's context and allows the backoff sleep to be cancelled.
127709.impact: Clients that rely on client-go (e.g., controllers, kubectl, custom operators) can now cancel backoff retries promptly and receive richer, context‑aware logs, improving responsiveness and debuggability.

128811.problem: Kubelet did not expose a dedicated HTTP endpoint that reports detailed runtime status (start time, uptime, Go version, binary version, compatibility version, etc.), making it harder for operators and monitoring systems to retrieve this information programmatically.
128811.affected: Cluster administrators, monitoring systems, and any tooling that needs to inspect kubelet runtime status.
128811.fix: Introduces a new `/statusz` HTTP endpoint on the kubelet that returns a human‑readable status summary, including start time, uptime, Go version, binary version, emulation version, and minimum compatibility version.
128811.impact: Operators and monitoring tools can now query kubelet for concise status information without needing to SSH into nodes or parse logs, improving observability, debugging, and automation workflows.

128818.problem: kube-scheduler did not expose its command-line flag settings via an HTTP endpoint, making it difficult for operators to inspect the configuration with which the scheduler was started.
128818.affected: Anyone running kube-scheduler who needs to view its runtime flag configuration, especially during troubleshooting and performance tuning.
128818.fix: Introduces a new `/flagz` HTTP endpoint on kube-scheduler that returns a plain‑text list of all flag names and their values used at startup.
128818.impact: Operators and developers can now quickly verify scheduler configuration without accessing pod logs or the process command line, improving debugging, observability, and reducing time to discover misconfigurations.

128824.problem: There was no HTTP endpoint to expose the command-line flags with which kube-controller-manager was started, making it difficult for operators and tooling to discover configuration at runtime.
128824.affected: Kubernetes clusters running the kube‑controller‑manager, especially operators, monitoring systems, and debugging workflows that need to know the component's flag configuration.
128824.fix: Introduces a new `/flagz` HTTP endpoint on the kube-controller-manager metrics server that returns the list of flag names and values in a human‑readable format.
128824.impact: Operators and debugging tools can now programmatically retrieve the controller‑manager's startup flags, improving observability, troubleshooting, and automated compliance checks without needing to access logs or the binary directly.

128950.problem: The kubectl autoscale command only interacted with the autoscaling/v1 API, preventing users from taking advantage of newer v2 features and requiring manual API selection.
128950.affected: Anyone using the `kubectl autoscale` subcommand, especially when working with clusters that support autoscaling/v2 or only support autoscaling/v1.
128950.fix: The command now attempts to use the autoscaling/v2 API first. If v2 is unavailable or returns an error, it gracefully falls back to the autoscaling/v1 API, preserving compatibility with older clusters.
128950.impact: Users can automatically benefit from v2 autoscaling capabilities (e.g., multiple metrics, refined scaling behavior) without breaking scripts or clusters that only support v1. The change improves usability and future‑proofs the CLI while maintaining backward compatibility.

128972.problem: There were no end-to-end tests covering volume group snapshot functionality, leaving the feature without regression protection.
128972.affected: Kubernetes developers, CI systems, and any workloads that rely on CSI group snapshot capabilities.
128972.fix: Added comprehensive e2e test suites for volume group snapshots to the Kubernetes test matrix.
128972.impact: Improves confidence in the stability of group snapshot implementations and helps catch regressions early in CI pipelines, benefiting storage developers and users of group snapshot features.

128985.problem: kube-proxy did not expose an HTTP endpoint to view the command‑line flags it was started with, making it difficult for operators to verify configuration and debug issues.
128985.affected: Cluster administrators and tools that need to inspect kube-proxy configuration; useful for debugging networking problems.
128985.fix: Introduced a new `/flagz` HTTP endpoint on kube-proxy that returns a plain‑text list of all parsed command‑line flags and their values.
128985.impact: Provides immediate visibility into kube-proxy's runtime configuration, simplifying troubleshooting, validation, and automated health‑checking of network components.

128987.problem: kube-scheduler did not expose a /statusz endpoint, so operators and tooling could not easily retrieve detailed runtime status (start time, uptime, Go version, binary version, compatibility info) for debugging and monitoring.
128987.affected: Cluster operators, monitoring systems, and any users needing scheduler runtime details.
128987.fix: Introduced a new /statusz HTTP endpoint on kube-scheduler that returns human‑readable status information, mirroring the statusz implementation used by other core components.
128987.impact: Provides administrators and observability tools with a simple way to query scheduler health and version details, improving troubleshooting and consistency across components.

128989.problem: kube-proxy did not expose a status endpoint, making it difficult for operators and tooling to retrieve runtime information such as start time, version, and health details.
128989.affected: Cluster administrators, monitoring agents, and any tooling that needs to query kube-proxy health or version information.
128989.fix: Introduced a new `/status` HTTP endpoint on kube-proxy that returns a concise status payload including start timestamp, uptime, Go version, binary version, emulation version, and compatibility version.
128989.impact: Provides immediate observability into kube-proxy, simplifying troubleshooting, health checks, and integration with monitoring systems. Improves operational visibility without needing to inspect logs or process state.

128991.problem: Cluster operators had no dedicated HTTP endpoint on kube-controller-manager to quickly retrieve runtime status such as start time, version, and compatibility information, making debugging and monitoring more cumbersome.
128991.affected: Users of kube-controller-manager (cluster operators, monitoring systems) who need runtime status information.
128991.fix: Introduced a new `/statusz` HTTP endpoint on kube-controller-manager that returns a concise status payload including start time, uptime, Go version, binary version, emulation version, and minimum compatibility version.
128991.impact: Provides operators and tooling with an easy way to query controller-manager health and version details, improving observability, simplifying troubleshooting, and enabling integration with external monitoring systems.

129028.problem: There were no built-in unit test helpers to validate CustomResourceDefinition CEL expressions and pattern rules, making it hard for developers to reliably test CRD validation logic.
129028.affected: Developers writing and testing CustomResourceDefinitions and validation logic, especially those using CEL or pattern validation.
129028.fix: Introduced new testing utilities that can be used in unit tests to evaluate CEL expressions and pattern constraints defined in CustomResourceDefinitions.
129028.impact: CRD developers can now write automated tests that verify validation behavior, improving test coverage and reducing the risk of invalid resources being accepted in clusters.

129072.problem: kubelet configuration files could contain an invalid `containerLogMaxFiles` value, leading to misbehaving logging or kubelet startup failures because the value was not validated.
129072.affected: Clusters where administrators set `containerLogMaxFiles` in the kubelet config. Invalid values would previously cause kubelet errors or uncontrolled log file creation.
129072.fix: Added validation logic in the kubelet config validator to check that `containerLogMaxFiles` is within the supported range and type, rejecting invalid configurations during startup.
129072.impact: Users configuring kubelet now get immediate feedback on invalid `containerLogMaxFiles` settings, preventing node crashes or uncontrolled log growth and improving cluster stability.

129119.problem: When a pod defines multiple required topologySpreadConstraints that share the same topologyKey, the PodTopologySpread plugin's PreFilter (and likely PreScore) overwrites counts instead of aggregating them, leading to incorrect pod counting and degraded scheduling performance.
129119.affected: Workloads that use required podTopologySpreadConstraints with duplicate topologyKeys; clusters where the scheduler processes many such pods may see performance regressions.
129119.fix: The scheduler plugin was updated to correctly aggregate pod counts for constraints with the same topologyKey, fixing the overwriting bug and optimizing the counting logic, which improves the scheduling speed for pods with required topology spreading.
129119.impact: Pods that rely on required topology spread constraints receive correct placement decisions and experience faster scheduling, preventing potential imbalance and reducing scheduler latency for affected workloads.

129271.problem: In dual‑stack clusters the single kube-proxy healthz/livez server (and associated metrics) did not differentiate between IPv4 and IPv6 sub‑proxies. Updates from either IP family overwrote the same data, causing health checks to appear healthy even if one family was failing and mixing metrics between families.
129271.affected: Clusters that enable dual‑stack networking with kube-proxy (including Linux and Windows nodes) where health checks or metrics are consumed.
129271.fix: The healthz and livez HTTP endpoints now extend their response schema to include the IP family (IPv4 or IPv6) for each reported item, allowing callers to distinguish health and metric information per family.
129271.impact: Operators can accurately monitor the health of each IP family and obtain correct per‑family metrics, preventing false‑positive health reports and misleading observability data. This improves debugging and reliability of dual‑stack deployments.

129278.problem: When the NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate is enabled, kubeadm upgrade left the `--container-runtime-endpoint` flag in `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env`, causing the kubelet to point to the wrong CRI socket.
129278.affected: Clusters that enable the NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate and perform a kubeadm upgrade.
129278.fix: kubeadm now removes the `--container-runtime-endpoint` flag from the kubelet flags file during an upgrade when the NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate is active.
129278.impact: Ensures the kubelet correctly uses the node‑local CRI socket after an upgrade, preventing kubelet start‑up failures or misrouted container runtime traffic.

129279.problem: When the NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate is enabled, kubeadm upgrade left the kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket annotation on the node, causing the node to retain an outdated CRI socket reference.
129279.affected: Clusters upgraded with kubeadm where the NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate is enabled; the affected nodes could experience mis‑configured CRI socket references.
129279.fix: During a kubeadm upgrade, kubeadm now automatically removes the kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket annotation from nodes that have the NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate enabled.
129279.impact: Prevents nodes from using a stale CRI socket annotation after an upgrade, ensuring the kubelet connects to the correct CRI socket and reducing upgrade‑related node failures.

129297.problem: When upgrading to Kubernetes 1.31+, the newly GA CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate redirects all operations for the in‑tree portworxVolume type to the external pxd.portworx.com CSI driver. If the Portworx CSI driver is not installed beforehand, volume provisioning, mounting, and other operations will fail, potentially disrupting workloads that use Portworx volumes.
129297.affected: Clusters that use the in‑tree portworxVolume storage class and rely on Portworx volumes. Workloads (pods, statefulsets, etc.) that mount Portworx volumes will be affected if the CSI driver is missing during upgrade.
129297.fix: The CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate is promoted to GA. Enabling it causes the control plane to route all portworxVolume actions to the external CSI driver. Users must install the Portworx CSI driver (pxd.portworx.com) on the cluster before performing the upgrade so that volume operations continue to work after the migration.
129297.impact: Ensures a smooth migration from the in‑tree Portworx volume plugin to the CSI driver, preventing runtime volume errors and possible application downtime during upgrades. Aligns Portworx storage with the GA CSI migration path used for other in‑tree drivers.

129334.problem: When the API server handled list requests with JSON output, it marshalled the entire list into memory before responding, causing high memory consumption and possible OOM failures for large collections.
129334.affected: Clients that perform list API calls expecting JSON responses, especially when the result set is large; the API server process itself.
129334.fix: Implemented streaming JSON list encoding: the server now marshals list items one at a time as they are written to the response. The behavior can be toggled off with the `StreamingJSONListEncoding` feature gate.
129334.impact: Reduces memory usage for list operations, enabling the API server to serve large collections more reliably and improving overall cluster stability and scalability.

129450.problem: kubeadm performed an unnecessary preflight check for the `nsenter` binary on Linux nodes, causing init/join to fail on systems where it was not installed. Conversely, it lacked a preflight check for `losetup`, which kubelet needs to keep block devices open, leading to kubelet failures when block devices are used.
129450.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to bootstrap clusters on Linux nodes, especially those that rely on block devices for storage.
129450.fix: Removed the `nsenter` preflight check from kubeadm on Linux nodes and added a new preflight check for the `losetup` binary, ensuring the required utility is present before proceeding.
129450.impact: Users can now run `kubeadm init` and `kubeadm join` on Linux nodes without `nsenter` installed, and nodes that need to manage block devices will be validated for `losetup` support, preventing kubelet runtime errors.

129583.problem: The behavior to honor a PersistentVolume's reclaimPolicy was behind the `HonorPVReclaimPolicy` feature gate, so clusters could not rely on consistent reclamation of volumes without manually enabling the gate.
129583.affected: Kubernetes clusters using PersistentVolumes, especially administrators who needed the reclaim policy behavior but had to enable the feature gate manually.
129583.fix: The `HonorPVReclaimPolicy` feature gate has been promoted to GA, making the functionality always enabled and removing the need for the gate flag.
129583.impact: All clusters now consistently apply the reclaimPolicy of PersistentVolumes, eliminating configuration drift and simplifying storage management for users and operators.

129589.problem: The EtcdLearnerMode feature gate remained in kubeadm after the feature had graduated to GA, requiring users to keep it enabled manually.
129589.affected: Clusters using kubeadm for installation or upgrade, particularly those upgrading to v1.32 where EtcdLearnerMode is now GA.
129589.fix: Removed the EtcdLearnerMode feature gate from kubeadm, as the feature is now always enabled by default.
129589.impact: Users no longer need to manage the EtcdLearnerMode feature gate during upgrades or new cluster creation, simplifying configuration and reducing potential confusion.

129591.problem: The ServiceAccountTokenNodeBinding feature was gated and disabled by default, requiring cluster operators to manually enable it to get the expected service account token binding behavior.
129591.affected: All clusters running kube-apiserver; any pods or workloads that rely on service account token node binding.
129591.fix: The feature gate is promoted to General Availability and locked to enabled, so the functionality is always on and no configuration is needed.
129591.impact: Clusters automatically gain the ServiceAccountTokenNodeBinding behavior, reducing configuration burden and ensuring consistent, secure handling of service account tokens across all workloads.

129620.problem: kubeadm health checks for control‑plane components were not using the address and port arguments defined in the static‑Pod manifests, which could cause the components to be reported as unhealthy even when they were reachable on a different address/port.
129620.affected: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm that have custom address/port settings for control‑plane static pods; administrators running kubeadm health‑check, init, join, or upgrade commands.
129620.fix: The WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate is graduated to Beta and kubeadm now extracts the bind address and port from each component’s static‑Pod manifest arguments when performing health checks.
129620.impact: Health checks performed by kubeadm (e.g., during init, join, or upgrade) now correctly reflect the real status of the API server, controller‑manager, and scheduler, reducing false‑positive/negative health reports and improving upgrade reliability.

129635.problem: When adding pods to a NodeInfo object, the scheduler recalculated pod resource requests each time, causing unnecessary CPU work and latency, especially when many pods remained unschedulable.
129635.affected: Clusters with high numbers of pending/unschedulable pods experience slower scheduling; the change benefits all workloads by making the scheduler more efficient.
129635.fix: The scheduler now caches the calculated pod resources during the AddPod operation in the scheduler framework, reusing the cached values for subsequent processing of the same pod.
129635.impact: Reduces CPU usage and speeds up the scheduling loop, leading to faster handling of large backlogs of unschedulable pods and overall scheduler performance improvement.

129656.problem: The fine‑grained kubelet authorization feature was only available as an optional alpha feature gate, so clusters had to manually enable it to get more granular permission checks for kubelet operations.
129656.affected: All nodes running the kubelet are affected; clusters that previously required manual enablement of fine‑grained authz will now have it on by default, improving security for workloads that interact with the kubelet.
129656.fix: The `KubeletFineGrainedAuthz` feature gate has been graduated to beta and is now enabled by default, activating fine‑grained authorization for kubelet without any extra configuration.
129656.impact: Clusters automatically gain tighter security for kubelet API calls, reducing the risk of over‑privileged access. Administrators no longer need to enable the feature gate manually, simplifying cluster hardening.

129688.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, limiting the use of newer language features, compiler improvements, and security updates.
129688.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, including all component binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.).
129688.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.24.0, updating the build toolchain to the latest supported Go release.
129688.impact: Improves binary performance, security, and maintainability. Developers rebuilding Kubernetes will need Go 1.24.0 installed, but runtime behavior for clusters remains unchanged.

129713.problem: Kubelet was still trying to set the .status.kubeProxyVersion field on its Node object, even though the field is being deprecated.
129713.affected: All clusters where kubelet runs and updates Node status; users or tooling that expected .status.kubeProxyVersion to be populated.
129713.fix: The DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion feature gate has been graduated and is now enabled by default, preventing kubelet from writing the kubeProxyVersion status field.
129713.impact: Node objects no longer contain a stale or unnecessary kubeProxyVersion status entry, reducing superfluous API writes and aligning node status with the deprecation of the field. Existing tools that consumed this field should not rely on it.
